checklist.step: Maintain the artefact inventory the archive is required to hold
actions: Open the REG-030 register in the Internal Regulatory System and list, for each writing entity, the artefact classes the archive must hold: 認可書, 届出 acknowledgement, as-filed 事業方法書 / 普通保険約款 / 算出方法書 version, 新旧対照表, 照会 thread, SERFF submission and disposition, and the annual statement schedules for the Art. 115 price fluctuation reserve, Art. 116 policy reserve and Art. 117 outstanding claims reserve.
For each class record its capture trigger, the owning team that hands it over, the mandatory metadata fields and the retention rule.
Reconcile the class list against the last FSA document request received so nothing the regulator has previously asked for sits outside the inventory.
Publish the inventory to Product Compliance, Regulatory Filing and the Statutory Reporting Manager as the handover contract.
checklist.done: the artefact inventory names every class, its trigger, owning team, metadata set and retention rule, and has been issued to the handover teams.

checklist.step: Capture the authorization letter the day it arrives
actions: On receipt of an 認可書 from the FSA Insurance Business Division or the Kanto Local Finance Bureau, scan or download the original and upload it to the compliance evidence repository under REG-030 / <entity> / <basic document> within one business day.
Record the metadata: 受付番号, application date, authorization date, issuing office, the basic document and clause authorized, and the effective date stated in the letter.
Attach the covering application (申請書) and 理由書 as lodged, so the letter and what it answers travel together.
Write the repository reference back onto the Internal Regulatory System register row and set the row to 'Archived'.
checklist.done: every received 認可書 is in the repository within one business day with 受付番号, authorization date and clause metadata, linked from its register row.

checklist.step: Capture notification acceptances and their acknowledgement numbers
actions: For each 届出 lodged, download the acceptance record showing the 受付番号 and acceptance date from the FSA electronic application and notification portal.
Pair the acceptance with the exact notified content — the 新旧対照表 and amended clause text as lodged, not a later working copy.
Where the notification was lodged on paper, scan the stamped receipt and record who lodged it and at which office.
File the pair in the repository under the same clause folder as any related authorization so the clause has one continuous history.
checklist.done: every notification has an archived acceptance with 受付番号 paired to the exact content lodged, filed under its clause folder.

checklist.step: Freeze and archive the as-filed version of each basic document
actions: At lodgement, take the 事業方法書, 普通保険約款 or 算出方法書 exactly as submitted and lock it as an immutable version in the document management repository with version id and lodgement date.
Attach the 新旧対照表 showing the prior authorized text against the filed text, clause by clause.
Record which product codes, riders and separate-account funds the version governs, and from which effective date.
Block further editing of that version — later amendments must open a new version rather than overwrite the filed one.
checklist.done: each lodged basic document exists as a locked, dated version with its 新旧対照表 and the product scope it governs.

checklist.step: Archive the reserve schedules that support the filed financial statements
actions: After each annual statement lodgement, take the price fluctuation reserve schedule showing, by asset class, the opening balance, the Ordinance for Enforcement Art. 65-2 accumulation rate applied, the base amount, the accumulation, any drawdown and the closing balance.
Take alongside it the Art. 116 policy reserve schedule and the Art. 117 outstanding claims reserve schedule including the incurred-but-not-reported component and its calculation basis.
Confirm each schedule ties to the lodged financial statements to the yen before archiving, and record the tie-out reference on the schedule cover.
Archive the set with the lodgement date, the fiscal year end and the general ledger extract identifier that produced it.
checklist.done: each lodged year has archived Art. 115, 116 and 117 schedules that tie to the filed statements with a recorded tie-out reference.

checklist.step: Archive every regulator correspondence thread against its parent filing
actions: For each 照会, additional-document request or SERFF objection, archive the item as received, the internal drafting thread, the clearance record and the lodged response with its receipt.
File the thread under the parent filing rather than in a correspondence folder of its own, so the filing history reads end to end.
Record the regulator reviewer name, the response due date and the actual lodgement date on the thread record.
Mark threads that changed a filed position, so the archive shows why the as-filed text differs from the originally drafted text.
checklist.done: every correspondence thread sits under its parent filing with reviewer, due date, lodgement date and any position change marked.

checklist.step: Enforce the mandatory metadata set at ingest
actions: Configure the REG-030 ingest form so entity, artefact class, basic document and clause, 受付番号 or SERFF tracking number, regulator date, fiscal year and retention class are all mandatory.
Reject uploads with an empty mandatory field back to the uploader rather than accepting them into a triage folder.
Run the weekly metadata-completeness report and send rows scoring below 100% back to the owning team with a two-business-day fix window.
Keep a controlled value list for artefact class and retention class so the archive stays queryable.
checklist.done: no REG-030 artefact can be ingested with a blank mandatory field and the weekly completeness report shows 100% on accepted items.

checklist.step: Store the archive on immutable media with controlled access
actions: Confirm the REG-030 repository area is configured write-once-read-many so an archived authorization or as-filed version cannot be edited or replaced in place.
Restrict write access to named Compliance Ops archivists and read access to Compliance, Regulatory Affairs, Actuarial, Internal Audit and Legal role groups.
Have the Identity Access Manager run a quarterly access recertification on those groups and remove leavers and role changers within five business days.
Evidence the immutability setting with a dated configuration export filed in the archive itself.
checklist.done: the archive is WORM-configured, access is limited to named role groups, and a dated configuration export plus recertification record exists.

checklist.step: Apply the retention label that matches the artefact class
actions: Apply 10-years-from-withdrawal to authorization correspondence and as-filed basic-document versions, so the record outlives the product it governs.
Apply 10-years-from-fiscal-year-end to the Art. 115, 116 and 117 reserve schedules and their supporting general ledger extracts, meeting the Companies Act Art. 432 accounting-book floor.
Apply life-of-contract-plus-5-years to any contract-level record filed under REG-030.
Run the label-coverage report monthly and fix unlabelled items before month end — an unlabelled item is eligible for silent deletion.
checklist.done: every archived artefact carries a retention label matching its class and the monthly label-coverage report shows no unlabelled items.

checklist.step: Reconcile the archive to the filing register every month
actions: Extract from the Internal Regulatory System every register row that reached a disposition in the month, by entity and jurisdiction.
Match each row to an archived artefact by 受付番号 or SERFF tracking number and list rows with no match.
For US rows corroborate the disposition independently in SERFF Filing Access rather than relying on the register field alone.
Chase every unmatched row with its owning team inside five business days and log rows still unmatched at month end as records exceptions.
checklist.done: the monthly reconciliation shows every disposed register row matched to an archived artefact, or the gap logged as an exception.

checklist.step: Run the annual inventory after the fiscal year end
actions: In April, after the 31 March fiscal year end, inventory the REG-030 archive by entity, artefact class and fiscal year.
Confirm the year's lodged annual statement, its Art. 115 / 116 / 117 schedules and every authorization received during the year are present.
Compare the inventory count to the prior year and investigate any class whose count fell without a matching business explanation.
Sign the inventory and file it in the archive as the year's completeness attestation.
checklist.done: a signed annual inventory exists showing the year's statements, reserve schedules and authorizations present, with count movements explained.

checklist.step: Prove retrieval against the clock before a regulator asks
actions: Twice a year pick ten artefacts at random across entities and classes — including one 認可書 older than five years and one price fluctuation reserve schedule from a prior fiscal year.
Time the retrieval from request to a readable, complete document and record the elapsed time against the 4-business-hour service standard.
Open each retrieved file and confirm it renders, is complete and matches its metadata rather than only that a file exists.
Report failures to the Head of Compliance the same day and open a reconstruction task for any unreadable or incomplete artefact.
checklist.done: a dated retrieval drill record shows ten artefacts retrieved, timed against the 4-hour standard and confirmed readable and complete.

checklist.step: Hold the disposal gate and apply legal holds
actions: Run the disposal proposal report before any scheduled destruction and route it to the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel for approval.

Suspend disposal on any artefact touched by an open FSA inspection, Local Finance Bureau request, market conduct examination, litigation or internal investigation, and record the hold reason and owner.
Confirm the disposal list contains no item whose parent basic-document clause is still in force before approving.
Record every destruction with the item id, retention rule satisfied, approver and date in the disposal register.
checklist.done: no artefact is destroyed without an approved disposal proposal, a clear legal-hold check and a disposal-register entry.

checklist.step: Assemble regulator document requests from the archive alone
actions: Log each incoming FSA or Local Finance Bureau document request with its scope, the named requester and its due date on the day it arrives.
Build the response pack from archived artefacts only — never from working copies held in team folders — and record each item's archive reference in the pack index.
Have Regulatory Counsel review the pack for completeness and privilege before it is produced, and minute that review.
File the produced pack and its index back into the archive so the company knows exactly what the regulator holds.
checklist.done: each request is answered from archived artefacts with an indexed pack, a counsel review and the produced pack filed back into the archive.

checklist.step: Escalate and reconstruct archive gaps
actions: Review every records exception raised in the month and rank them by inspection exposure — a missing 認可書 for an in-force clause ranks above a missing internal drafting note.

For each gap direct a reconstruction route: request a certified copy from the issuing office, retrieve from the counterparty or the SERFF public record, or document an attestation of what was filed with the evidence relied on.
Set a closure date and name the owner, and report any gap touching an in-force basic-document clause to the Compliance Committee.
Sign off the closure only when the reconstructed artefact is archived with full metadata.
checklist.done: every records gap has a ranked exposure, a named reconstruction route and owner, and closure signed off only on an archived, fully described artefact.

testing.step: Build the population of filings and statements that should be in the archive
actions: Extract from the Internal Regulatory System every REG-030 register row reaching a disposition in the period — authorizations, notification acceptances, SERFF dispositions — by entity and jurisdiction.
Add the period's lodged annual and interim statements from the Statutory Reporting calendar so the reserve schedules fall into the population.
Reconcile the extract to the product release notes and to the SERFF Filing Access disposition list for the US entities, clearing every difference before sampling.
Have the extractor sign the population as complete and record the query, filters and run timestamp in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to release notes, the statutory calendar and SERFF dispositions, and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to the archive in both directions
actions: Match every population row forward to an archived artefact on 受付番号 or SERFF tracking number and list the unarchived rows.
Run the match backwards from the archive index to the register and list archived artefacts with no register row — these signal filings made outside the register.
Quantify both gap directions as counts and percentages of the population.
Treat every unmatched row in either direction as an automatic exception with no judgement applied.
testing.done: both directions of the register-to-archive reconciliation are complete with gaps quantified and listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of authorizations (認可書) received in the period and 100% of lodged annual statements carrying the Art. 115 reserve schedule.
Take 25 further artefacts by seeded random selection across notification acceptances, correspondence threads and as-filed versions, with a minimum total of 40 items.
Deliberately include at least five artefacts older than five years to test aged retrieval, and record why they were added.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is drawn covering all authorizations and lodged statements plus a seeded tail including aged artefacts.

testing.step: Retrieve each sampled artefact and time it
actions: Request each sampled artefact through the normal repository route with no advance notice to Compliance Ops.
Record the request time and the time a readable, complete document was in hand, and compare to the 4-business-hour standard.
Open every retrieved file and confirm it is legible, complete to the last page and free of DRAFT watermarks.
Record failures separately as 'not retrievable' and 'retrieved but deficient' — the two carry different root causes.
testing.done: every sampled artefact has a timed retrieval record and a legibility and completeness result against the 4-hour standard.

testing.step: Verify the authorization artefacts against the regulator's own record
actions: For each sampled 認可書 confirm the archived copy carries the issuing office, 受付番号, authorization date and the specific basic document and clause authorized.
Compare the clause named in the letter to the as-filed version archived alongside it, and confirm the 新旧対照表 covers exactly that clause.
For US rows re-open the SERFF filing on its tracking number and confirm the archived disposition matches the disposition SERFF shows today, including the disposition date.
Treat a mismatch between the archived and the regulator-held disposition as an exception even where the archived copy is the more favourable one.
testing.done: every sampled authorization matches its as-filed version and, for US rows, the disposition held in SERFF today.

testing.step: Re-perform the price fluctuation reserve schedule from the archived support
actions: Take the archived Art. 115 price fluctuation reserve schedule for the sampled fiscal year and the general ledger extract identified on its cover.
Recompute the accumulation for two asset classes by applying the Ordinance for Enforcement Art. 65-2 rate for that class to the archived base amount, and compare to the recorded accumulation.
Trace any drawdown to the realized-loss support archived with the schedule and confirm the drawdown does not exceed the realized loss it offsets.
Tie the closing balance to the lodged financial statements line and note any difference to the yen.
testing.done: the sampled year's reserve schedule recomputes from archived support and ties to the lodged statements, or the difference is quantified.

testing.step: Test metadata completeness and index accuracy
actions: For each sampled artefact compare the recorded metadata — entity, artefact class, clause, 受付番号, regulator date, fiscal year, retention class — against the document's own face.
Search the archive by 受付番号, by basic-document clause and by fiscal year and confirm each search returns the sampled artefact.
Score metadata completeness and accuracy separately; a complete but wrong 受付番号 is an accuracy failure, not a completeness one.
List any artefact findable only by browsing folders as an indexing exception.
testing.done: each sampled artefact is confirmed findable by 受付番号, clause and fiscal year with metadata scored for completeness and accuracy.

testing.step: Test immutability, access and the disposal gate
actions: Obtain the repository configuration export and confirm the REG-030 area is WORM-enabled with the retention labels applied at the class level.
Attempt, with the Document Management Specialist observing, to overwrite one archived test artefact and record that the platform refuses it.
Review the quarter's access recertification evidence and confirm write access is limited to named archivists and that leavers were removed within five business days.
Read the disposal register for the period and confirm every destruction had an approved proposal, a clear legal-hold check and no item whose parent clause remains in force.
testing.done: immutability is evidenced by a refused overwrite, access is confirmed restricted and recertified, and every disposal is supported by an approved proposal.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception carrying the artefact id, entity, class, what is missing or wrong and the inspection exposure it creates.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — handover missed at disposition, metadata not enforced, storage misconfigured, retention label absent, premature disposal — and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any missing artefact touching an in-force basic-document clause, open a reconstruction task with Regulatory Affairs the same day.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the archive completeness rate, the metadata accuracy score and the retrieval performance against the 4-business-hour standard.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind each finding, calling out separately any gap on an in-force clause.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Compliance Ops and holds no write access to the archive, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any in-force-clause gap to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper under REG-030 / records assurance.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states completeness, metadata accuracy and retrieval performance, the conclusion and the committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Capital Management owns the quarterly and annual solvency margin ratio calculation under Insurance Business Act Art. 130 and the parallel economic value-based solvency ratio, with the Appointed Actuary owning the Art. 116 policy reserve and Art. 117 outstanding claims reserve inputs that feed it.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Insurance Business Act Art. 130 (solvency margin ratio) with Ordinance for Enforcement Arts. 86 and 87 and FSA Public Notice No. 50 of 1996 (margin components and the R1–R8 risk formula) re-read at each quarter close; Art. 117 and Ordinance Art. 73 re-read for the outstanding claims and IBNR input; NAIC RBC instructions for the US entities and the BMA BSCR instructions for Bermuda.

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly and annual capital adequacy production for every regulated entity: Japan solvency margin ratio under Art. 130, the FY2025-onward economic value-based solvency ratio (ESR), NAIC RBC for the US writing companies, and BSCR / SCR where the group holds Bermuda or EU entities — including the Variable Annuity minimum-guarantee (最低保証) risk charge.

In-scope systems.value: Liability and minimum-guarantee risk runs in the actuarial modeling platform; asset data from the investment book of record; the margin and risk build assembled against the closed general ledger and lodged through the statutory reporting pack.

Compliance procedure documented.value: Capital Adequacy Calculation Procedure — data freeze and reconciliation, margin component build (capital, price fluctuation reserve, contingency reserve, unrealized gains at their prescribed inclusion rates, subordinated debt, prescribed deductions), R1–R8 risk build, the Art. 130 aggregation formula, sensitivity runs, review chain and lodgement.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Risk Officer with the Chief Actuary's technical concurrence; re-approved annually and within 30 days of any FSA public notice changing the margin components, the risk factors or the ESR standard.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly ratio produced within 30 days of each quarter end for internal and supervisory reporting; the annual ratio for the 31 March fiscal year end goes into the 事業報告書 within 3 months of year end and into the Art. 111 説明書類 within 4 months; US RBC is filed with the NAIC annual statement by 1 March.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Close calendar tasks at data freeze (working day 3), first-run review (working day 8), Appointed Actuary review (working day 14), CFO and CRO sign-off (working day 20) and lodgement (working day 30), with automatic escalation to the Head of Capital Management on any missed gate.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Input data extracts, model run logs with version and parameter set, the margin and risk build workbook, sensitivity results, the Appointed Actuary opinion and the sign-off pack retained 10 years from the fiscal year end under Companies Act Art. 432.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Calculation errors, unapproved model or parameter changes, late lodgement and any breach of the 200% supervisory threshold are logged with root cause, restatement scope, the prompt-corrective-action implication and a named remediation owner.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CFO signs off every restatement of a lodged ratio and every remediation of a calculation control failure, with the Chief Risk Officer countersigning where the correction moves the ratio by more than 10 percentage points.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every solvency ratio calculation produced in the period across all regulated entities — four Japan quarterly Art. 130 runs, the annual run lodged in the 事業報告書, the parallel ESR run, and the NAIC RBC and BSCR/SCR submissions — together with their input extracts and model runs.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Recomputation must agree to the lodged ratio within 1 percentage point with every larger difference explained to source; zero tolerance on an unapproved model or parameter change, on an unreconciled general ledger tie-out, and on lodgement after the statutory date; any ratio below 200% is a reportable event regardless of test outcome.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly and annual; the independent test runs each quarter on that quarter's run with a deeper annual test covering the lodged 事業報告書 ratio, the ESR run, full input reconciliation and the model change history for the year.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Capital Management, must not have built or run any sampled calculation, and must hold no write access to the model parameter set.

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly capital adequacy test workpaper (input reconciliations, independent recomputation, margin component walk, risk-charge re-performance, sensitivity comparison, exceptions) filed in the compliance evidence repository under REG-030 / capital adequacy.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The lodged ratio with the full margin and R1–R8 component build, the reconciliation to the closed general ledger, the model version and parameter set, sensitivity results and the Appointed Actuary opinion — producible for an FSA 立入検査 or an NAIC financial examination within 5 business days.

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs owns the channel to the FSA Supervisory Bureau and the Kanto Local Finance Bureau; the Head of Capital Management answers technical questions on the build; a ratio below 200% is reported to the FSA and the Board the same day under the prompt corrective action (早期是正措置) framework before any external comment is made.

checklist.step: Freeze the valuation date data and confirm the close is final
actions: Confirm with the Controller in writing that the general ledger for the quarter or the 31 March fiscal year end is closed and that no further journals will post, and record the close timestamp.
Take the trial balance extract for every regulated entity and lock it as the capital run's source, naming it <entity>-TB-<valuation date>.
Take the in-force policy extract from the policy administration system and the investment position extract from the investment book of record at the same valuation date and cut-off time.
Reject any extract whose as-at timestamp differs from the ledger close and re-request it rather than adjusting it by hand.
checklist.done: the ledger is confirmed closed and locked trial balance, in-force and investment extracts all carry the same valuation date and cut-off.

checklist.step: Reconcile the input extracts to the ledger and to the reserve schedules
actions: Reconcile the in-force extract policy count and sum insured to the policy administration control report and clear differences to the policy.
Reconcile the investment extract market value and book value by asset class to the ledger investment balances and to the custodian statement.
Reconcile the Art. 116 policy reserve and the Art. 117 outstanding claims reserve — including the incurred-but-not-reported component — from the reserving schedules to the ledger liability balances.
Publish a signed reconciliation sheet showing every difference, its explanation and whether it is accepted or corrected, and hand it to the Capital Model Actuary.
checklist.done: in-force, investment and reserve inputs reconcile to the ledger with every difference explained on a signed reconciliation sheet.

checklist.step: Build the total solvency margin numerator component by component
actions: Pull from the closed ledger: capital and capital reserve, retained earnings, the price fluctuation reserve balance under Art. 115, the contingency reserve (危険準備金), the general allowance for doubtful accounts and any qualifying subordinated debt.

Add unrealized gains at the prescribed inclusion rates — securities gains included at the prescribed percentage with losses taken in full, and land revaluation gains at their own prescribed rate — quoting the FSA public notice paragraph beside each rate used.
Add the excess of the continued Zillmerized reserve over the recorded reserve and any deferred acquisition-related item permitted by the notice.

Apply the prescribed deductions — intangible fixed assets, deferred tax assets above the allowed limit, holdings of other financial institutions' capital instruments — and show each deduction on its own line.
Foot the numerator and tie every component to a named ledger account or schedule reference; leave no plug line.
checklist.done: the total solvency margin foots from named ledger accounts and schedules with each inclusion rate and deduction cited to the public notice.

checklist.step: Compute the insurance risk charges R1 and the third-sector charge
actions: Run the insurance risk (保険リスク) calculation over the frozen in-force extract using the risk coefficients set in the FSA public notice for each product class and the applicable risk amount base.
Run the third-sector insurance risk charge separately over the medical, cancer and long-term care blocks using its own prescribed coefficients and the prescribed stress basis.
Print the run log showing model version, parameter set id, run date and record counts, and reconcile the run's in-force record count to the frozen extract.
Hand the component results to the Capital Model Actuary with the coefficient table used attached, not merely referenced.
checklist.done: the insurance and third-sector risk charges are produced from the frozen in-force extract with a run log, record-count tie and the coefficient table attached.

checklist.step: Compute the assumed interest rate risk and the minimum guarantee risk
actions: Compute the assumed interest rate risk (予定利率リスク) by comparing the guaranteed crediting rates in force against the prescribed benchmark yield, over the policy reserve base defined in the public notice.

Compute the minimum guarantee risk (最低保証リスク) for the Variable Annuity block, choosing between the standard method and the alternative method permitted by the notice and recording which was used and why.

For the standard method apply the prescribed charge to the guaranteed benefit amount net of separate-account value; for the alternative method attach the stochastic run specification, scenario count and calibration date.
Reconcile the separate-account values used to the unit-pricing records at the valuation date.
Document any method change from the prior quarter with the Chief Actuary's written concurrence before it enters the build.
checklist.done: interest rate and minimum guarantee risk charges are computed on a named, documented method with separate-account values tied to unit pricing.

checklist.step: Compute the asset management risk from the investment position
actions: Classify every holding at the valuation date into the public notice's asset categories — domestic equities, foreign currency assets, bonds by credit grade, real estate, loans, derivatives and off-balance-sheet exposures.
Apply the prescribed risk factor to each category, apply the credit risk factors by counterparty rating, and compute the concentration add-on where a single issuer exceeds the prescribed limit.
Compute the derivative exposure on the prescribed basis rather than on notional, and show the netting applied with the master agreement relied on.
Reconcile the total classified market value back to the investment extract and to the ledger before releasing the charge.
checklist.done: the asset management risk charge is built from a fully classified holdings list that reconciles to the investment extract and the ledger.

checklist.step: Aggregate the risks through the Art. 130 formula and compute the ratio
actions: Assemble the component results and apply the prescribed aggregation — the square root of the sum of squares of the correlated risk groupings, plus the asset management risk and the catastrophe component, then the business management risk at its prescribed percentage of the aggregate.
Compute the ratio as total solvency margin divided by one half of total risk, expressed as a percentage to one decimal place.
Rebuild the aggregation once in an independent workbook from the same component inputs and confirm the two agree before releasing a number to anyone.
Produce the movement analysis against the prior quarter, splitting the change into margin movement, risk movement, new business, market movement and method or parameter change.
Flag immediately to the Head of Capital Management if the ratio falls below 250% so the trajectory is visible well before the 200% supervisory threshold.
checklist.done: the ratio is computed, independently rebuilt to agreement, and explained by a movement analysis split into margin, risk, new business, market and method effects.

checklist.step: Run the required sensitivities and the reverse test
actions: Run the standard sensitivities: a parallel interest rate shift, a domestic equity fall, a yen appreciation against the foreign currency book, a credit spread widening and a lapse shock on the Variable Annuity block.
Record the ratio under each sensitivity beside the base ratio in the sign-off pack.
Run the reverse test to find the equity fall and the rate shift at which the ratio would reach 200%, and state both as headroom figures.
Hand the headroom figures to the Chief Risk Officer and the Chief Investment Officer for the capital and hedging discussion, not merely for filing.
checklist.done: the sign-off pack carries the standard sensitivities and the market movements that would take the ratio to 200%, issued to the CRO and CIO.

checklist.step: Evidence model governance for every model and parameter used
actions: Confirm each model used in the run is registered in the model governance repository with a current validation date and no expired validation.
List every parameter and coefficient change since the prior run and confirm each carries a dated approval from the Chief Actuary or the model owner.
Confirm the run used the approved production version — compare the run log version string to the repository's approved version, not to the modeller's assertion.
Log any unapproved change as a control exception the same day and hold the sign-off until it is resolved.
checklist.done: every model is validated and current, every parameter change is approved and dated, and the run version matches the approved production version.

checklist.step: Obtain the Appointed Actuary's review of the liability inputs
actions: Review the Art. 116 policy reserve and the Art. 117 outstanding claims reserve, including the incurred-but-not-reported component, as they enter the capital build.

Confirm the reserves meet the standard policy reserve requirement — the prescribed standard mortality table and standard interest rate for the issue-year cohorts to which it applies — and that any company-specific basis is documented.
Confirm the future cash-flow analysis supporting reserve adequacy is current and note any block requiring an additional reserve.
Sign the liability input section of the sign-off pack, naming any reservation, before the ratio is released for CFO approval.
checklist.done: the Appointed Actuary has signed the liability inputs with the standard-reserve basis confirmed and any reservation named.

checklist.step: Produce the parallel economic value-based solvency ratio
actions: Value assets and liabilities on the economic basis using the prescribed discount curve with its ultimate forward rate and volatility adjustment as published for the valuation date.
Compute available capital as economic assets less the best estimate liability and the risk margin, and compute the required capital from the prescribed stress modules.

Compute the ESR and reconcile it to the Art. 130 statutory ratio, explaining the drivers of the gap — discounting basis, contract boundary treatment, risk margin and the treatment of the price fluctuation and contingency reserves.
Present both ratios side by side to the Chief Risk Officer so capital decisions are not taken on the statutory ratio alone.
checklist.done: an ESR is produced on the prescribed economic basis and reconciled to the statutory ratio with the drivers of the gap explained.

checklist.step: Produce the overseas capital calculations on the same close
actions: For the US writing companies compute NAIC risk-based capital from the annual statement data, completing the RBC formula pages by risk category and deriving total adjusted capital and the authorized control level.
Compute the ratio to the authorized control level and check it against the company action level trigger before the statement is finalised.
For any Bermuda entity produce the BSCR schedules on the BMA basis, and for any EU entity produce the SCR with its quantitative reporting templates.
Reconcile every overseas calculation back to the same closed ledger used for the Art. 130 build so the group tells one story.
checklist.done: each overseas entity's capital calculation is produced from the same closed ledger and checked against its own supervisory action trigger.

checklist.step: Take the ratio through the sign-off chain
actions: Review the sign-off pack: base ratio, margin and risk component build, ledger reconciliation, movement analysis, sensitivities and headroom, model governance confirmation and the Appointed Actuary's signed liability section.
Obtain the Chief Risk Officer's countersignature on the risk build and the headroom figures.
Challenge and minute any component moving more than 10% from the prior quarter without an explanation in the movement analysis.
Sign the pack and release the ratio for lodgement and disclosure; an unsigned pack does not go out.
checklist.done: the CFO has signed a complete pack countersigned by the CRO, with every material component movement explained on the record.

checklist.step: Lodge and disclose the ratio on the statutory timetable
actions: Place the annual solvency margin ratio and its component table into the 事業報告書 for lodgement within 3 months of the 31 March fiscal year end and into the Art. 111 説明書類 within 4 months.
Lodge the quarterly ratio through the supervisory reporting route within 30 days of quarter end and record the submission reference.
File the US annual statement with its RBC pages with the NAIC and the domiciliary state by 1 March and capture the filing confirmation.
Check the disclosed figure character by character against the signed pack before publication — a transcription error in a disclosed ratio is a disclosure failure.
checklist.done: the ratio is lodged and disclosed on each jurisdiction's statutory date with submission references captured and the published figure verified against the signed pack.

checklist.step: Monitor the threshold and act before it is breached
actions: Track the ratio against the internal early-warning level set above the 200% supervisory threshold and review it at each monthly capital committee with the latest market movement applied.

Where a projection shows the ratio reaching the early-warning level within two quarters, direct the management action — reinsurance, hedging, asset de-risking, subordinated issuance or new business restriction — with an owner and a date.
On any actual fall below 200%, report to the FSA and the Board the same day and prepare the improvement plan required under the prompt corrective action (早期是正措置) framework.
Minute every threshold discussion and its decision in the capital committee record and carry it to the Board through the board portal.
checklist.done: the ratio is tracked against an early-warning level above 200% with a dated, owned management action for any projected approach and same-day reporting on any actual breach.

testing.step: Build the population of capital calculations produced in the period
actions: List every solvency calculation produced in the period by entity and basis — the Japan Art. 130 quarterly and annual runs, the parallel ESR run, NAIC RBC and any BSCR or SCR.
Add the input extracts, model run logs and sign-off packs behind each so the population covers the production chain and not only the headline number.
Reconcile the list to the close calendar and to the lodgement register so no run produced and then abandoned is left out.
Have the extractor sign the population as complete and record the run identifiers in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population lists every calculation with its inputs, run logs and sign-off pack, reconciled to the close calendar and lodgement register.

testing.step: Reconcile the calculation inputs back to the closed ledger
actions: Take the trial balance the run claims as its source and compare its close timestamp to the Controller's close confirmation for that period.
Tie the capital, price fluctuation reserve, contingency reserve, policy reserve and outstanding claims reserve figures used in the margin build to the ledger balances line by line.
Tie the investment market values used in the asset management risk charge to the ledger and to the custodian statement at the same valuation date.
Treat any input taken from a pre-close extract or adjusted outside the ledger as an exception, whatever its size.
testing.done: every material calculation input ties to the closed ledger at the correct valuation date, or the difference is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of components to re-perform
actions: Take 100% of the annual lodged Art. 130 run and 100% of any run whose ratio fell below 250%.
From the quarterly runs select every margin component and risk charge exceeding 5% of the total, plus five smaller components chosen by seeded random selection.
Include the Variable Annuity minimum guarantee charge in every period regardless of size, given its method optionality.
Record the seed, the selection rule and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers the annual run, all components above 5% of total, the minimum guarantee charge and a seeded random tail.

testing.step: Recompute the margin numerator independently
actions: Rebuild the total solvency margin in an independent workbook from the ledger balances, without opening the preparer's file first.
Apply the inclusion rates for unrealized securities and land gains straight from the FSA public notice text and confirm losses were taken in full rather than at the gain rate.
Recompute each prescribed deduction — intangibles, deferred tax above the limit, holdings of other financial institutions' capital — and compare line by line to the preparer's build.
Investigate every difference to source and record it as an error, a presentation difference or a documented judgement.
testing.done: the margin numerator is independently rebuilt and agrees to the lodged build, with every difference resolved to source and classified.

testing.step: Re-perform the insurance, interest rate and minimum guarantee risk charges
actions: Take the frozen in-force extract and apply the public notice coefficients for two product classes by hand to a defined sub-block, comparing to the model output for the same sub-block.
Recompute the assumed interest rate risk for one cohort from its guaranteed crediting rate, the prescribed benchmark and the policy reserve base.

Recompute the minimum guarantee charge under the standard method on a defined set of Variable Annuity contracts, and where the alternative method was used confirm the stochastic specification, scenario count and calibration date were approved before the run.
Tie the model's in-force record count and total risk amount back to the frozen extract to prove no records were dropped.
testing.done: each re-performed risk charge agrees to the model output within tolerance and the model's record counts tie to the frozen extract.

testing.step: Recompute the aggregation and the published ratio
actions: Rebuild the aggregation from the component results using the prescribed correlated groupings, the additive asset management and catastrophe components and the business management risk percentage.
Recompute the ratio as total solvency margin over one half of total risk and compare to the published figure to one decimal place.
Compare the published figure in the 事業報告書 and the Art. 111 説明書類 character by character to the signed sign-off pack.
Treat a difference above 1 percentage point that cannot be explained to source as a fail, and any difference between the signed pack and the published figure as a disclosure exception.
testing.done: the recomputed ratio agrees within 1 percentage point and the published figure matches the signed pack exactly.

testing.step: Test the reserve inputs and the Appointed Actuary's review
actions: Confirm the Art. 117 outstanding claims reserve fed into the build includes the incurred-but-not-reported component computed on the ordinance basis and not omitted for the interim quarters.

Confirm the Art. 116 policy reserve used the prescribed standard mortality table and standard interest rate for the cohorts subject to the standard policy reserve, and that any company basis is documented.
Read the Appointed Actuary's signed liability section and confirm it names the reserves reviewed, the adequacy analysis relied on and any reservation.
Treat an unsigned or generically worded liability section as a control failure rather than a documentation observation.
testing.done: the reserve inputs are confirmed on the prescribed bases and the Appointed Actuary's signed section names the reserves, the analysis and any reservation.

testing.step: Test model governance and the change history for the period
actions: Compare the model version string in each sampled run log to the approved production version in the model governance repository.
List every parameter and coefficient change made during the period and confirm each has a dated approval that pre-dates the run it first affected.
Confirm no model used had an expired validation at the run date, and quantify the ratio impact of any that did.
Treat any run executed on an unapproved version or parameter set as an exception requiring the ratio impact to be quantified, not merely noted.
testing.done: every sampled run used an approved, currently validated model version and parameter set, or the exception is quantified in ratio terms.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception carrying the entity, run identifier, component affected, the ratio impact in percentage points and whether a lodged figure is affected.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — input taken pre-close, wrong inclusion rate, coefficient table out of date, unapproved parameter change, aggregation error, late lodgement — and name an owner.

Where a lodged or disclosed ratio is misstated, open a restatement assessment with the Chief Financial Officer and Regulatory Affairs the same day and record whether a supervisory notification is required.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with its ratio impact, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the recomputation difference against the 1-percentage-point tolerance, the input reconciliation result and the on-time lodgement result for every entity.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind each finding, calling out separately any period in which the ratio approached 200%.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Capital Management, built no sampled calculation and holds no write access to the model parameter set, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any restatement and any threshold proximity to the Audit Committee and the Board at their next sitting, and file the signed workpaper under REG-030 / capital adequacy.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the recomputation difference, reconciliation and lodgement results, the conclusion and the committee reporting date.
